ArXiv cs.AI.title: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.06962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Proof assistants such as Lean check mathematical proofs down to the axioms, and AI agents have recently made writing such proofs cheap. We describe AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory, together with the functional analysis it rests on, has been autoformalized by AI agents. A machine-checked proof certifies only the formal statement it proves, so the remaining human task is to confirm that each formal statement says what was intended. ArXiv cs.AI.title: KDASO: Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization for Liability Adjudication Tasks
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.06972v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Liability adjudication tasks (e.g., legal charge determination) require analyzing event descriptions against domain-specific skills to determine whether a party should bear liability. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in this area by leveraging executable skills for interpretable reasoning, existing approaches face three critical limitations: skill libraries become stale as real-world scenarios dynamically evolve, skill descriptions often suffer from a semantic execution gap where LLMs deviate from intended expert logic, and

ArXiv cs.AI.title: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Geometry
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.06977v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reproducible LLM inference requires that a request produces the same output regardless of the other requests in the batch. Existing solutions pay for this in different ways: batch-invariant kernels constrain every operator, and isolating prefill with fixed-shape decode ({our CoRun-style baseline}) gives up shared prefill compute and pads decode. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Resource-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Post-Training through Elastic Expert Parallelism
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.06984v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning post-training improves the capabilities of large language models, but generating training responses is a major computational bottleneck. In mixture-of-experts models, workers that finish their assigned responses may remain occupied because their experts are still needed by workers processing longer responses. Consequently, approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline occurs after local response generation finishes. ArXiv cs.AI.title: The Two-Ledger Model: Transaction-Grain Cost Accounting for Multi-Agent AI Systems Across Clouds, Models, and Systems of Record
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.06989v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprises run business transactions through multi-agent AI systems spanning clouds, large language models (LLMs), orchestration harnesses, and systems of record. Finance receives AI cost only at settlement grain, aggregated by SKU and charge period. The business question (what did this order, claim, or case cost in AI?) cannot be answered from billing data, because providers never see enterprise transaction boundaries. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Autonomous AI Agents Systematically Diverge From Human Preferences in Proof Formalization
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.06995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have ushered in a new age of proof abundance, but helping humans understand these proofs requires new attention to the differences in how AI agents and humans pursue a proof-making task. We present "simulated collaboration", a methodology that allows us to examine two key questions: (1) the relative attention AI agents pay to surface syntax or, conversely, deeper underlying semantics, and (2) how and where AI agent preferences for what to do next diverge from human preferences. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI with Empirical Characterization of Policy Behavior and Parameter Sensitivity
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.06996v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The policy that converts runtime estimates of an autonomous agent's condition into operational authority is rarely specified or measured. We empirically characterize the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP), which maps an Authorization Readiness Score (ARS), a weighted combination of runtime trust, operational stability, and contextual risk, onto discrete authorization levels through an asymmetric rule: escalation requires consecutive observations above a band edge plus a margin, while a sharp drop in readiness restricts authority at onc

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.07048v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evolution has shaped intelligence for billions of years. Artificial intelligence (AI) now raises a striking possibility: intelligence may begin to direct its own evolution. As AI agents become capable of modifying and evaluating their own behavior, how quickly could they improve, and how can that improvement remain safe? We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution following environmental change. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement and Self-Calibration
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.07051v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Once an agent is live, teams want to know whether it is doing its job, not just whether it throws errors. Yet most evaluation is one-off: a benchmark run, a look at traces, a single score. Its conclusions neither check themselves nor reach the agent. We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.07066v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discovering cooperative behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of joint state-action spaces, which hinders the emergence of coordinated behaviors from trial-and-error alone. Intrinsic rewards are often used to aid discovery, but naively combining them with team objectives can distort the learning signal, compromising task performance. ArXiv cs.AI.title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.07073v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A verified Dafny postcondition certifies that a formula holds, but it does not guarantee that the result was reached through genuine independent reasoning. We introduce a cross-agent formalization protocol where a Specifier model translates clinical trial criteria into a Dafny predicate, and an Implementer model writes an operational method checked against it. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.07088v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic models offer a powerful account of cognition, but their scope has historically been limited by the need for hand-engineering and computational tractability. We show how advances in artificial intelligence (AI) can scale symbolic modeling and help overcome these engineering limitations. We introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS)---an approach for automated search of interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs that verifiably reproduce behavior---and apply it to model both human and machine behavior across hundreds of

ArXiv cs.AI.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.07123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for evaluating the behavior of chatbots and other AI systems. In deployment, however, their agreement with the intended human evaluation policy may degrade as user interactions and score distributions change. Existing automatic prompt optimization methods are primarily studied as one-shot procedures on static development sets and therefore provide limited guidance for maintaining LLM judges over time. We frame this problem as judge drift and introduce PromptOps, a closedloop

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Goal Revelation as a Bridge Between Information-Theoretic Empowerment and Capability-Based Human Power
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.07247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Power matters for AI safety. Optimal agents tend to acquire power across a wide range of objectives (instrumental convergence). As we embed AI agents into socio-technical systems, humans risk gradual disempowerment. Both concerns call for a formal, quantitative measure of power. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Robust Ranking of Port Impacts from Impending Tropical Cyclones: A Two-Stage Recommendation System
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.07296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When a tropical cyclone (TC) threatens several ports, preparedness planning depends on anticipating which ports are likely to be affected and where disruptions may last longest. Limited historical observations at individual ports and uncertainty in landfall location make these relative impacts difficult to estimate. We use a two-stage recommendation framework that first selects candidate ports based on their proximity to the expected landfall location and then ranks them by their estimated number of impact days. ArXiv cs.LG.title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.06953v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Steel property models can perform well on random test splits even when they extrapolate poorly to unfamiliar alloys. SteelAgent couples metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with a language-model interface for property prediction, uncertainty reporting and inverse design. We examine how the choice of held-out unit changes the conclusions drawn from SteelBench tensile-strength evaluations. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.06956v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems explore in parallel by spawning sub-agents with isolated context windows, whereas single-agent systems append every search and verification step into one growing trajectory. However, existing multi-agent frameworks duplicate prefix KV caches across branches, exchange findings by re-prefilling text summaries, and flatten or drop cross-branch dependencies during reinforcement learning (RL).

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.06979v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: M/EEG source imaging requires accurate localization and reliable uncertainty estimates, yet posterior credible regions are rarely assessed for empirical calibration. We present a simulation-based framework for uncertainty quantification and calibration of empirical Bayesian inverse methods with closed-form conditional Gaussian posterior summaries. We compare Bayesian minimum norm (BMN) with sLORETA depth weighting and sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) with sparse basis field expansions (S-FLEX). ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.06988v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Forecasting foundation models are increasingly used as frozen feature extractors for time series classification, but it remains unclear whether their pretrained representations offer an advantage over strong classifiers that do not require pretraining. This raises an important question: do these representations provide useful information beyond what the model architecture alone can capture, particularly when labelled data are scarce? ArXiv cs.LG.title: Robust Stream Classification using Time Neutralising Decision Trees
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.06991v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Data Streams are characterised as a potentially infinite source of data subject to non-stationarity. This non-stationarity, also called Concept Drift, often results in deployed predictive models having to be perpetually retrained as the underlying data generating process of the stream changes over time. Drift Detectors are a class of methods used to identify these changes, triggering these retraining procedures. Historically, Stream Learning has operated under the assumption that instances are only seen once, and cannot be stored for later use.

ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07025v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive decoding relies on the KV cache, whose memory footprint grows linearly with context length and caps batch size and throughput. Existing post-training methods exploit redundancy across tokens, layers, and feature dimensions, or lower numerical precision. We identify a complementary axis: within each attention head, values are largely predictable from their corresponding keys. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07065v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper develops a stochastic dynamical-systems perspective on three classes of generative AI models. First, we formulate large language models (LLMs) as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models with attention-based dependencies. This formulation connects pretraining by conditional maximum likelihood to sequential token generation and provides a probabilistic interpretation of LLM operation. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07069v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) is computationally challenging due to the curse of long-range dependence on history. Fortunately, recent studies have shown that a range of POMDPs that satisfy the filter stability assumption can be well approximated by a superstate Markov Decision Process (MDP) based on a truncated history in a finite-memory window, with a value gap that decays with the window length. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07071v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose Mechanistic Shaping, a unified framework for shaping models through their internal representations. Mechanistic Shaping is applied during training so that models follow specifications (rules) about which concepts they express, measured via their outputs or internal representations (e.g., no harmful content), and also which concepts they rely on, i.e., what they use to make their decisions (e.g., not a candidate's gender when screening a r\'esum\'e). ArXiv cs.LG.title: Optimistic Hedge in General-Sum Games: Fundamental Limits and Regret Bounds via Temporal Approximation
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07078v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Optimistic Hedge, a multiplicative weight update with one step of extrapolation, is one of the most natural regret-minimizing dynamics for games, and characterizing its regret has been a longstanding open question. Daskalakis, Fishelson and Golowich proved that if all $m$ players in a finite general-sum game follow Optimistic Hedge with a fixed learning rate, each player's regret is polylogarithmic in the horizon $T$. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07093v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly recognized for their remarkable capabilities; federated learning (FL) offers a promising framework for collaboratively fine-tuning LLMs on edge devices while achieving data privacy. However, edge devices are inherently heterogeneous: clients may exhibit diverse data distributions and resource constraints, including limited memory and computation budgets. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A challenge to Weight Space Learning as it expands from task specific and vision models to Large Language Models (LLMs) is the absence of a well curated and analyzed LLM population. To address this, we train such a model zoo for application to Weight Space Generation by systematically varying the data mixture composition between web text, books, mathematics, coding, and French across populations of 51M, 124M, and 355M parameter GPT-2 Models, each tier with count N = 100. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07122v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Profit-maximizing Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand (AMoD) operators may exploit consumer surplus through excessive prices and underserve less profitable regions by relocating vehicles away from them. We study how penalty-based regulation of an AMoD operator in a multimodal mobility system can limit surge pricing and improve regional service availability. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07124v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine-learning models predicting live birth after in vitro fertilisation (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) from routine clinical data report performance from near chance to near perfect. We systematically reviewed these models under PRISMA 2020, searching OpenAlex, Scopus and Web of Science to 22 October 2026, appraised them with PROBAST+AI and TRIPOD+AI, and pooled their discrimination with random-effects meta-analysis on the logit scale. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.07125v1 Announce Type: new

The Verge AI.description: Meta will now allow you to build customized, app-like experiences within its Muse AI assistant. The new feature, called "spaces," allows Muse to build things like a shopping hub, school dashboard, music tracker, trivia game, and more, which you can interact with directly in the app. If you connect your space to a relevant app, […]

The Verge AI.description: When Irene moved to San Francisco last year, she started using dating apps as a way to meet new people, get to know her new city, and connect with others who care about the things she does. The Verge AI.description: On Tuesday, millions of American voters went to the polls and voted overwhelmingly for Democrats and against AI. The fight against Big Tech is about to come roaring back, and the fight over data centers is looking even harder for the folks trying to build them. On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David […]

The Verge AI.description: inMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog, Native Instruments, and more, has decided to embrace the modding community. The Verge AI.title: Amazon will let you text Alexa your shopping list
The Verge AI.description: Amazon is adding a new feature to Alexa for Shopping that allows customers to purchase items by texting the AI shopping assistant. Users can describe the products they're looking to buy and/or provide a photograph of the item, and Alexa for Shopping will search for matching results in Amazon listings, text back with recommendations, and […]

The Verge AI.title: Protesters break into Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam
The Verge AI.description: Protesters have broken into a construction site of a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam this morning. Members of the Geef Tegengas group helped organize the protest against the construction of three 85-meter data center towers in the outskirts of Amsterdam. Reuters reports that around 100 people made it into the construction site, with some […]

The Verge AI.title: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
The Verge AI.description: Following this week's midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won't use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials. Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions […]

The Verge AI.title: Airbnb is working on an AI travel agent
The Verge AI.description: Airbnb plans to roll out an AI agent in the first half of 2027 that will help users plan and book travel, the company said in its Q3 2026 earnings shareholder letter released today. "Today's AI agents are good at simple, routine tasks, like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment," Airbnb said. "But […]

The Verge AI.title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
The Verge AI.description: Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup's new always-on "Teammates" can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use. Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer, an AI system that can deploy agents on your device […]

The Verge AI.description: Meta now lets you have voice conversations with your Muse AI agent in real time, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced today. The feature has been rolled out to me, and I gave it a spin on the iOS app while writing this article. As you chat with your Muse agent, the avatar at the top of […]

Wired AI.title: Free Chinese AI Models Are Getting Scary Good at Hacking
Wired AI.description: An experiment in which AI models were asked to break into simulated networks showed the hacking skills of DeepSeek and GLM to be not far behind OpenAI’s most advanced cyber model, which isn’t public.

Wired AI.title: AI Companies Really, Really Want to Buy Your Work Files and Emails
Wired AI.description: Data brokers are collecting all sorts of internal corporate files to help train AI models. Not everyone is thrilled.

Wired AI.title: Ads in Chatbots Have Arrived. Here’s What’s Working—and What’s Not
Wired AI.description: As Anthropic maintains its vow to keep ads out of Claude, the rest of the AI chatbot industry is racing to win over advertisers without antagonizing users.

Wired AI.title: Reddit Founder Says Building Social Media Apps Is ‘Not Cool Anymore’
Wired AI.description: Alexis Ohanian is trying to figure out what’s next for user-generated content now that so much of the internet is “compromised.”

Wired AI.title: Exclusive: Aina’s Smart Ring Wants to Be a Remote Control for Your AI Agent
Wired AI.description: The startup Aina bets you won’t need to rely on your phone to control virtual assistants. It’s making a smart ring that lets you control the actions of your autonomous agents with one tap.

Wired AI.title: Finding New Drugs Is Laborious. This AI Startup Is Skipping The Lab Work
Wired AI.description: Potential Sciences, a startup backed by the UK government, is betting that training AI models on computer-generated biochemical data can speed up the plodding process of developing new drugs.

Wired AI.title: AI’s Next Trick? Speaking Dolphin
Wired AI.description: Denise Herzing, the founder and director of the Wild Dolphin Project, is using AI to help understand audio and video footage of the marine mammals.

Wired AI.title: He Trolls AI Labs for a Living. Now They All Want to Work With Him
Wired AI.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceXSI have all reached out to Husk, an influencer who regularly goes viral by exposing the shortcomings of chatbots.

Wired AI.title: The Blue Wave Has Tech Bros Scrambling for Data Centers in Space
Wired AI.description: After Democrats won big in Texas and other AI infrastructure hot spots on Tuesday, data center enthusiasts looked for comfort in low Earth orbit.

Wired AI.title: The Biggest Pro-AI Super PAC Network Didn’t Really Impact the Midterms
Wired AI.description: Leading the Future, backed by Silicon Valley’s biggest billionaires, had a war chest of $100 million and an aggressive stance against AI regulation. All of it didn’t add up to much on Tuesday night.

MIT News — AI.title: How to predict the behavior of molecules from scant data
MIT News — AI.description: A machine-learning approach called CheMeleon provides a practical way to develop new drugs or other molecules with much less detailed, expensive experimentation.

MIT News — AI.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory
MIT News — AI.description: A new system identifies and corrects unreliable object descriptions stored in a robot’s memory, improving the robot’s ability to interact with its environment.

MIT News — AI.title: Building connections across the research infrastructure
MIT News — AI.description: MIT.nano and the Northeast Microelectronics Coalition gathered facility leaders and technology professionals from across the nation to explore ways to make shared-access facilities more connected.

MIT News — AI.title: Powering up for a pivotal moment
MIT News — AI.description: From a nuclear revival to qubits, the MIT Energy Initiative’s annual research conference tracked deployment of today’s technologies to discovery of tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

MIT News — AI.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
MIT News — AI.description: The MIT professors collaborated to identify the first AI-discovered antibiotic, a scientific breakthrough that is widely recognized as a milestone in AI-driven drug discovery.

MIT News — AI.title: MIT affiliates named 2026 Schmidt Sciences AI2050 Fellows
MIT News — AI.description: Five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni are honored with fellowships to advance research on beneficial AI.

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
MIT News — AI.description: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata discuss a new project to track how AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

MIT News — AI.title: 3 Questions: Why infrastructure is entering a defining era
MIT News — AI.description: Professor Ali Jadbabaie describes how AI, digital transformation, climate change, and complex geopolitics are forcing engineers and policymakers to rethink how infrastructure is designed, built, and managed.

MIT News — AI.title: Making machines that can listen
MIT News — AI.description: Professor Paris Smaragdis develops computers with superhuman hearing for applications like speech recognition, music understanding, and environmental monitoring.

MIT News — AI.title: Learner collaborates with MIT peers to develop book of AI insights
MIT News — AI.description: Prabha Jha used her experience with MIT Open Learning’s program for senior executives to develop AI solutions for her employer, Verizon, and to write a book.

MIT News — AI.title: At New York Climate Week 2026, MIT connects with a global network
MIT News — AI.description: A cross-section of the MIT community convened discussions on topics ranging from data centers and super pollutants to agriculture and education.

MIT News — AI.title: At MIT, Martha Minow speaks on sustaining democracy, both by using and overcoming AI
MIT News — AI.description: In Compton Lecture, the distinguished legal scholar warns of potential “loss of the Enlightenment” while suggesting ways innovations can meet our civic and cultural needs.

MIT News — AI.title: Reinforcing the value of human understanding at MIT
MIT News — AI.description: During the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences’ 75th Anniversary Symposium, President Sally Kornbluth said “MIT has never needed your particular insight and guidance more than we do now.”

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the “messy” human mind
MIT News — AI.description: Assistant Professor Benjamin Lindquist studies how engineers deliberately injected randomness into early AI, giving rise to deep-learning models that sometimes hallucinate.

MIT News — AI.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices
MIT News — AI.description: “X-Hinges” helps design and 3D print items like lamps and gloves with an interactive twist: automatically embedded sensors that perceive and adaptively respond to human contact.
